method: surrogate-peptide LC-MS/MS (signature peptide FTITAGSK) on human liver S9 from the University of Washington human liver bank; each liver measured in singlet on three separate days
as_reported: nmol FABP1 per mg S9 protein, extrapolated to liver expression using the HLS9 yield
conversion: the SOURCE's own: tissue expression divided by the liver fraction of intracellular water, fICW = 0.573, with tissue density taken as 1 mL/g. Not recomputed here
location: Results, prediction of individual human liver Kp values; Figure 5C and Table S3-1
note: The largest direct quantification of human hepatic FABP1 found. Independent corroboration of the order: McCarty & Guengerich 2025 (J Biol Chem 301:108168) state FABP1 is 7-11% of liver cytosolic protein, reaching up to 1 mM, which brackets this mean and maximum. A preprint of the same work is at doi 10.64898/2026.01.17.700130; the peer-reviewed JPET version is cited here

method: clinical reference interval, not a single study
conversion: divided by 66,463 g/mol, the albumin molar mass used throughout this project
note: DELIBERATELY A RANGE, NOT A POINT. No single study is cited because none is needed: the comparison this feeds is reported across the whole interval so the conclusion can be read against it. A point estimate here would be false precision in the one input that varies most between people
